properties.name: Sumer (Sumerian City-States)
properties.description: Earliest urban civilization in southern Mesopotamia, comprising city-states like Ur, Uruk, Lagash, and Nippur.

properties.name: Old Kingdom Egypt
properties.description: Age of pyramid building. Unification of Upper and Lower Egypt under pharaonic rule.

properties.name: Indus Valley Civilization
properties.description: Bronze Age civilization in the Indus River basin, featuring cities with advanced urban planning and drainage.

properties.name: Xia Dynasty
properties.description: First dynasty of ancient China according to tradition. Existence partially confirmed by archaeology.

properties.name: Akkadian Empire
properties.description: World's first empire, founded by Sargon of Akkad. United Sumerian city-states under centralized rule.

properties.name: Hittite Empire
properties.description: Major Anatolian power that rivaled Egypt. Signed one of history's first known peace treaties at Kadesh.

properties.name: Old Babylonian Empire
properties.description: Height under Hammurabi, who codified one of the earliest law codes. Controlled much of Mesopotamia.

properties.name: New Kingdom Egypt
properties.description: Egypt's imperial age. Expanded into Nubia and the Levant. Pharaohs included Ramesses II and Tutankhamun.

properties.name: Shang Dynasty
properties.description: First historically confirmed Chinese dynasty. Known for oracle bones, bronze casting, and earliest Chinese writing.

properties.name: Kingdom of Kush
properties.description: Nubian kingdom south of Egypt. Conquered and ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty. Known for pyramid-building at Meroe.

properties.name: Zhou Dynasty
properties.description: Longest-reigning Chinese dynasty. Gave rise to Confucius, Taoism, and the Hundred Schools of Thought.

properties.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
properties.description: Dominant power of the ancient Near East. Famous for brutal military campaigns and the royal library at Nineveh.

properties.name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
properties.description: Babylon's final imperial period. Nebuchadnezzar II destroyed Jerusalem and built the Hanging Gardens.

properties.name: Kingdom of Macedon
properties.description: Northern Greek kingdom that became the dominant Greek power under Philip II and then Alexander the Great.

properties.name: Athens & the Delian League
properties.description: Birthplace of democracy. Led the Delian League against Persia and produced Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle.

properties.name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
properties.description: Largest empire the world had yet seen. Founded by Cyrus the Great, stretching from Egypt to Central Asia.

properties.name: Macedonian Empire (Alexander)
properties.description: Alexander the Great's empire at its peak, stretching from Greece to northwestern India.

properties.name: Seleucid Empire
properties.description: Successor state to Alexander's empire in the east. Controlled the Fertile Crescent and much of the Iranian plateau.

properties.name: Maurya Empire
properties.description: First empire to unify most of the Indian subcontinent. Ashoka spread Buddhism throughout Asia.

properties.name: Qin Empire
properties.description: China's first unified imperial dynasty. Built the Great Wall and standardized weights, measures, and writing.

properties.name: Roman Republic
properties.description: Rome's republican period, expanding from a city-state to dominate the Mediterranean world.

properties.name: Han Dynasty
properties.description: Golden age of Chinese civilization. Opened the Silk Road, advanced science and bureaucracy.

properties.name: Parthian Empire
properties.description: Iranian empire that controlled the Silk Road between Rome and China. Defeated Roman armies at Carrhae.

properties.name: Roman Empire
properties.description: The classical Mediterranean superpower at its height under Trajan. Spread Roman law, Latin, and Christianity.

properties.name: Kushan Empire
properties.description: Major Silk Road empire linking Rome, Persia, India, and China. Important center for Buddhism's spread.

properties.name: Kingdom of Aksum
properties.description: Ethiopian trading empire that controlled the Red Sea trade. One of the first states to adopt Christianity.

properties.name: Gupta Empire
properties.description: Golden Age of India. Advances in mathematics (zero, decimal system), astronomy, literature, and philosophy.

properties.name: Byzantine Empire
properties.description: Eastern Roman Empire that preserved Roman and Greek culture for a millennium. Center of Orthodox Christianity.

properties.name: Sassanid Persian Empire
properties.description: Last great pre-Islamic Persian empire. Rival of Rome and Byzantium. Zoroastrianism as state religion.

properties.name: Western Roman Empire
properties.description: The western half of the Roman Empire after the 395 split. Fell to Germanic migrations in 476 CE.

properties.name: Tang Dynasty
properties.description: Often considered China's golden age of culture, trade, and military power. Chang'an was the world's most cosmopolitan city.

properties.name: Umayyad Caliphate
properties.description: Largest Islamic empire at its time, stretching from Spain to Central Asia. Spread Arabic language and Islam rapidly.

properties.name: Abbasid Caliphate
properties.description: Islamic Golden Age. Baghdad's House of Wisdom preserved and advanced science, mathematics, and philosophy.

properties.name: Carolingian Empire
properties.description: Charlemagne's empire, the first major Western European polity since Rome. Predecessor of France and Germany.

properties.name: Khmer Empire
properties.description: Southeast Asian empire centered in Cambodia. Built Angkor Wat, the world's largest religious monument.

properties.name: Song Dynasty
properties.description: China's first gunpowder weapons, movable type printing, and advanced commerce. Lost northern China to the Jin.

properties.name: Kingdom of England
properties.description: English kingdom that conquered Wales and Ireland. Magna Carta (1215) established constitutional governance principles.

properties.name: Kingdom of France
properties.description: France under the Capetian, Valois, and Bourbon dynasties. Major European power through the medieval and early modern eras.

properties.name: Holy Roman Empire
properties.description: Loose confederation of Central European states. At its height under Charlemagne; famously 'neither holy, Roman, nor an empire'.

properties.name: Mali Empire
properties.description: West African empire that controlled trans-Saharan gold and salt trade. Mansa Musa was reputedly the wealthiest person in history.

properties.name: Byzantine Empire (Late)
properties.description: Much diminished Byzantine state after the Fourth Crusade's sack. Finally fell to the Ottoman Turks in 1453.

properties.name: Mongol Empire
properties.description: Largest contiguous land empire in history at its peak. United Eurasia, enabling trade and cultural exchange across the Silk Road.

properties.name: Delhi Sultanate
properties.description: First major Islamic sultanate in India. Repelled the Mongol invasion and introduced Persian administrative culture.

properties.name: Yuan Dynasty (Mongol China)
properties.description: Mongol rule over China. Marco Polo visited under Kublai Khan. Connected China to the wider Mongol world.

properties.name: Ottoman Empire (Early)
properties.description: Rising Anatolian Turkish state that gradually conquered Byzantine territory before taking Constantinople in 1453.

properties.name: Great Zimbabwe / Mutapa
properties.description: Stone-city civilization in southern Africa. Major gold-trading state linked to Swahili coast merchants.

properties.name: Ming Dynasty
properties.description: Chinese dynasty that expelled the Mongols, built the Forbidden City, and sent Zheng He's treasure fleets across Asia and Africa.

properties.name: Kingdom of Portugal
properties.description: Pioneer of European maritime exploration. Established the first sea route to India and built a global trading empire.

properties.name: Crown of Castile & Aragon
properties.description: United Spanish kingdoms under Ferdinand and Isabella. Funded Columbus's 1492 voyage and began the conquest of the Americas.

properties.name: Ottoman Empire (Peak)
properties.description: At its height under Suleiman the Magnificent, the empire spanned three continents and was the most powerful state in the world.

properties.name: Safavid Empire
properties.description: Established Shia Islam as Iran's official religion. Persian cultural renaissance. Constant rival of the Ottoman Empire.

properties.name: Songhai Empire
properties.description: Largest empire in West African history. Timbuktu was a major center of Islamic scholarship and trade.

properties.name: Oyo Empire
properties.description: Yoruba empire in West Africa, dominant in the region's politics and the Atlantic slave trade.

properties.name: Mughal Empire
properties.description: Dominated the Indian subcontinent for over three centuries. Built the Taj Mahal; peak GDP rivaled all of Europe.

properties.name: Spanish Colonial Americas
properties.description: Spain's vast colonial empire in the Americas, including Mexico, Central America, and most of South America.

properties.name: Colonial Brazil (Portugal)
properties.description: Portuguese colony in South America. Became the largest country in Latin America upon independence.

properties.name: Tsardom of Russia
properties.description: Centralized Russian state under Ivan the Terrible. Expanded eastward into Siberia and established autocratic rule.

properties.name: Qing Dynasty (China)
properties.description: China's last imperial dynasty, founded by Manchu conquerors. Largest extent of Chinese territory in history.

properties.name: Kingdom of Great Britain
properties.description: Union of England and Scotland. Became a major colonial power and began the Industrial Revolution.

properties.name: British India (Company Raj)
properties.description: East India Company control over the Indian subcontinent, gained through trade and conquest over the 18th century.

properties.name: United States of America (Early)
properties.description: Newly independent republic expanding westward. Purchased Louisiana (1803) and drove westward expansion.

properties.name: Gran Colombia
properties.description: Bolívar's short-lived united republic of northern South America, which dissolved into Venezuela, Colombia, and Ecuador.

properties.name: Russian Empire
properties.description: Peter the Great transformed Russia into a European power. Catherine the Great expanded it to become the world's largest state.

properties.name: First French Empire (Napoleon)
properties.description: Napoleon's France dominated continental Europe. Spread revolutionary ideals but ultimately fell to the Sixth Coalition.

properties.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
properties.description: World's leading naval and industrial power through the 19th century. The British Empire became the largest in history.

properties.name: German Confederation
properties.description: Loose association of German states after Napoleon's defeat. Prussia and Austria competed for dominance.

properties.name: Austrian Empire
properties.description: Habsburg multi-ethnic empire that dominated Central Europe after Napoleon's defeat, including Hungary, Bohemia, and northern Italy.

properties.name: Russian Empire (1815–1885)
properties.description: Europe's largest power. Expanded into Central Asia and the Caucasus. Defeated Napoleon and dominated post-Congress Europe.

properties.name: Ottoman Empire (1815–1885)
properties.description: The 'sick man of Europe' — Ottoman power declined as nationalist movements in Greece, Serbia, and Bulgaria gained independence.

properties.name: European Coastal Africa (Colonies)
properties.description: European powers controlled coastal trading posts in Africa before the Scramble for Africa (1885).

properties.name: United States (Westward Expansion)
properties.description: The US after the Mexican-American War gave it California and the Southwest. Completed transcontinental railroad 1869.

properties.name: German Empire
properties.description: Unified Germany under Prussian leadership. Rapid industrialization made it Europe's most powerful land power.

properties.name: Austria-Hungary
properties.description: Dual monarchy created by the Ausgleich (Compromise) of 1867. A multi-ethnic empire of 11 nationalities.

properties.name: Argentina
properties.description: Declared independence from Spain in 1816. One of Latin America's largest and most prosperous nations.

properties.name: Ecuador
properties.description: Emerged from the dissolution of Gran Colombia. Named for its location on the equator.

properties.name: Meiji Japan
properties.description: Rapid modernization following the Meiji Restoration. Japan industrialized and reformed within a generation.
